Cancellation Policy:

Once a reservation is booked, it is non-refundable. 

Change Policy:

No permit changes are allowed once the reservation is completed. You may cancel and rebook the reservation.
description.comment_box_description: This permit reservation is only for the portion of your trip within Canyonlands National Park (below Potash or Mineral Bottom Boat Ramps), if your full trip starts somewhere else (i.e. Green River State Park) please provide the date and location here. Note, you will need a separate permit from the BLM for the Green River above Mineral Bottom.
description.description:
Canyonlands National Park is a wilderness of countless canyons and fantastically formed buttes carved by the Colorado River and its tributaries. Rivers divide the park into four districts: Island in the Sky, The Needles, The Maze, and the rivers themselves. The park preserves the natural beauty and human history throughout its four districts. While they share a primitive desert atmosphere, each offers different opportunities for wildness and solitude.

The Colorado and Green Rivers have played a significant role in shaping the landscape of Canyonlands. Seeing the park from the bottom up affords a unique perspective. Above their confluence at the heart of Canyonlands, the rivers offer miles of flatwater perfect for canoes, sea kayaks and other shallow-water boats. A commercial upriver shuttle is necessary for non-motorized boats. Below the confluence, the combined flow of both rivers spills down Cataract Canyon with remarkable speed and power, creating a fourteen-mile stretch of Class III to V whitewater. It is a particularly hazardous and isolated section of the Colorado River, subject to extreme water level fluctuations, for experienced river runners only.
description.driving_directions: Canyonlands National Park Headquarters and the Backcountry Permit Office are located off of US Highway 191, at 2282 SW Resource Blvd. Moab UT 84532.
description.edu_video_alt_text: Welcome to Canyonlands National Park.  This video explains the wilderness character of Canyonlands National Park that protected it as one of America's most prized places.
description.edu_video_title: Canyonlands National Park Backcountry Orientation Video: Terra Incognita
description.fee_policy:
Permit Reservation Fee: There is a non-refundable $6.00 reservation fee for each permit. 

Recreation Fee: There is a $10 per person fee for Cataract Canyon trips only.

Entrance Fee: The park charges an entrance fee which you may pay upon arrival or purchase a few days in advance. The park also honors valid annual or lifetime America the Beautiful-the National Parks and Federal Recreational Lands Passes (e.g. Senior, Military, 4th Grade, etc.) also known as interagency passes. For more information visit the park's Fees & Passes web page.
description.need_to_know_email:
• This is NOT your permit (this is a reservation confirmation). Print your permit (or download it to a mobile device) from your user profile. The permit must be in the trip leader’s possession at all times, is valid only for the selected date and does not allow travel on the Colorado River above the Potash Boat Ramp or on the Green River above Mineral Bottom.
  • Backcountry Permit Office: canyres@nps.gov, 435-259-4351.
  • Regulations and Required Equipment. The trip leader and all participants must read, understand and comply with River Regulations including equipment (flotation devices, trash and waste disposal containers, etc.) and rules on campfires, pets, aquatic invasive species, boat registration, etc.
  • Boat Takeout Information. Cataract Canyon takeouts are challenging due to low lake water levels. Hite Ramp is closed. Cataract Canyon boaters may takeout at Halls Crossing Ferry Ramp, approximately 50 miles down lake from North Wash (anticipate 10+ hours with a motor). North Wash Ramp (AKA Dirty Devil) takeout is primitive, undeveloped dirt, is very steep with loose gravel and a swift river current. You will not be able to back a trailer down the takeout slope; boaters will need to carry all gear and boats up the slope. Takeouts here are congested and time consuming and may result in damage to equipment or injury to people. Collaborate with other boaters as you near Lake Powell to work out takeout times.
  • Entrance Fee. We encourage you to pay the entrance fee in advance since launch points are all outside the park boundary. The park also honors America the Beautiful-the National Parks and Federal Recreational Lands Passes (e.g. Senior, Military, 4th Grade, etc.). 
  • Change and Cancellation Policy. No permit changes are allowed once the reservation is booked. You must cancel and rebook. Please notify the park as soon as possible if you decide not to use your permit. Fees are non-refundable.
description.need_to_know_order:
Contact the Backcountry Permit Office via email (canyres@nps.gov ) or phone (435-259-4351) with any questions or concerns.

  • You are booking a single day trip permit that allows a group to travel on the river(s) only for the day you selected. The permit does not allow overnight use. For overnight use, book an Overnight River Permit. 

  • River access points are few and all are outside the park boundary.  

  • The permit does not allow travel on the Colorado River above the Potash Boat Ramp or on the Green River above Mineral Bottom. River maps are available at the Park Store. 

  • The trip leader is responsible for ensuring all participants read and understand all park River Regulations which cover required equipment (flotation devices, trash and human waste disposal, etc.) and other important topics (campfires, pets, etc.). All boaters will travel the flatwater sections (inc. Cataract Canyon boaters) and must read the park's Flatwater web page and watch the accompanying video. Cataract Canyon boaters must additionally view the Cataract Canyon web page and video.

  • Cataract Canyon is a challenging stretch of river at all water levels and is only recommended for experienced boaters familiar with the rivers in Canyonlands National Park. You must have a motorized boat to complete Cataract Canyon in a day (and to complete most Flatwater trips as well). 

  • This permit may be issued for noncommercial or commercial users. You must have a National Park Service Commercial Use Authorization to lead commercial trips.

  • All motorized boats must be registered, including those from out-of-state. Motorized boats must have valid state registration, decals, placards, and a serviceable fire extinguisher. Boats with out-of-state registration are allowed on Utah waters for 60 days per calendar year (hull numbers are required).

  • Before launching, follow Utah state law requirements to prevent the spread of Aquatic Invasive Species (such as Quagga Mussels).
description.need_to_know_permit:
Who needs a Day Use River Permit? Canyonlands National Park requires a permit for all boats entering the park on the Green and Colorado Rivers. Each group (1-40 people) will need to have a permit (printed or digital) in their possession.

BEFORE YOU RESERVE YOUR PERMIT:

  • Most day trips require motorized boats.

  • Review the Canyonlands Boating Information Guide and River Regulations. For more trip planning information, visit the Boating page and/or contact the Backcountry Permit Office (email canyres@nps.gov or call ((435) 241-3110).

  • Review the information on the web pages listed below and watch the mandatory video. If you plan to boat through Cataract Canyon, also read the Flatwater web page and watch the Flatwater video since you cannot bypass the flatwater sections on your way to Cataract Canyon.

    • Flatwater. Flatwater day trips are not easy to coordinate and are only for those with well-planned out itineraries or motorized boats. There are very limited river access points (all outside the park boundary).

    • Cataract Canyon. Cataract Canyon is a challenging stretch of river at all water levels. You must have a motorized boat to complete Cataract Canyon in a day.

These permits are only for experienced boaters familiar with the rivers in Canyonlands National Park.

OTHER THINGS TO KNOW BEFORE YOU BOOK YOUR RESERVATION:  

  • This permit is for day use only on the date you select. This permit does not permit you to camp in the river corridor in Canyonlands National Park. Book an Overnight River Permit if you plan to camp along the river.

  • A river permit requires that you follow the River Regulations which specify mandatory equipment, requirements for human waste disposal, PFDs, Food/Trash Storage and disposal, campfires and more.

Launch Points. When you book your trip, you must enter your launch and take-out points. Access points are limited and are all located outside of the park boundary. Read more about launch points and takeouts in the park’s Boating Information Guide. Day use river permits do not allow travel on the Colorado River above the Potash boat ramp or for travel on the Green River above Mineral Bottom boat ramp. River maps are available through the Canyonlands Park Store.

  • Flatwater trips on the Green River often launch from Green River State Park, Ruby Ranch or Mineral Bottom. Flatwater trips on the Colorado River typically use the Potash or Moab boat ramps.

  • Cataract Canyon) trips launch from Potash, Moab, Green River State Park or Mineral Bottom.

Motorized Boats Required for Cataract Canyon and Recommended for Flatwater. Cataract Canyon is a challenging stretch of river at all water levels and is only recommended for experienced boaters. You must have a motorized boat to complete Cataract Canyon (and most other river trips) in a day.

Motorized Boat Registration and Equipment. All motorized boats, including out-of-state boaters, must have valid state registration, decals, placards, and a serviceable fire extinguisher. Boats with out-of-state registration are allowed on Utah waters for 60 days per calendar year; hull numbers are required.

Know the laws on Invasive Aquatic Species (Quagga Mussels). View Aquatic Invasive Species in Utah for more information.

Commercial Trips: You must have a Commercial Use Authorization to lead commercial trips. Contact canyres@nps.gov for more information.

Park Entrance Fee. The park charges an entrance fee which we encourage you to purchase a few days in advance since all launch points are outside the park. The park also honors valid annual or lifetime America the Beautiful-the National Parks and Federal Recreational Lands Passes (e.g. Senior, Military, 4th Grade, etc.) also known as interagency passes. For more information visit the park's Fees & Passes web page.
description.no_show_policy: Reservations are not refundable. Please notify the park Backcountry Office as soon as possible if you decide not to use your permit (email canyres@nps.gov or call (435) 241-3110)
description.quota_details: The number of people per group is limited to 40 to minimize the impact to the rivers, wildlife, and experiences of solitude.
description.season_information:
A day use river permit is required year-round for all boating day trips on the Green and Colorado Rivers and Cataract Canyon (up to a maximum of 40 people). This permit does not permit you to camp overnight in the river corridor. Due to the difficult logistics associated with taking out on the Green and Colorado Rivers, consider an overnight river trip.

Reservations for the entire calendar year open on January 1. You can print or download your permit 7 days before your trip. Permits are available both online and in person. Any permits not reserved online will be available in person at the Backcountry Permit Office in Moab during Operating Hours & Seasons. There is no fee for day use permits obtained in person.

62174702.description:
• Cataract Canyon contains 14 miles of rapids ranging in difficulty from Class III to V Whitewater . It is a particularly hazardous and isolated section of the Colorado River and is subject to extreme water level fluctuations. 

  • All boaters are advised to read the Canyonlands Boating Information Guide before their trip.

  • Campsites are first come, first serve. The character of the river changes dramatically depending on the season. During high water, camps can be difficult to find, especially for large groups. River users are encouraged to register for camps below the Confluence. For more information on campsites click here .  

  •  Some take-outs are primitive and unimproved. Boaters should be aware of lake conditions .
